title: Lines 99–114
subtitle: The goddesses discuss a plan to unite Aeneas and Dido in marriage

units.en: 'Why don't we work together instead, for a lasting peace, and a marriage sealed between them? You have exactly what you set your whole heart on: Dido is burning with love, the madness has taken hold right through to her bones. Let us, then, rule this one people jointly, with equal authority between us; let her be allowed to serve a Trojan husband, and hand her Tyrians over [to you|32,35] as her dowry.'

units.en: Venus knew well enough that Juno had spoken with false intent, meaning to turn the kingdom of Italy aside to the shores of Libya instead, and [answered|15,16] her in turn: 'Who would be mad enough to refuse an offer like that, or choose to [go to war|25,26] with you — if only fortune [follows through on|33,31] what you propose?

units.en: But I am carried along uncertain by the fates, not knowing whether Jupiter wants one single city for both Tyrians and the exiles from Troy, or would approve of the two peoples mixing, their nations joined by treaty. You are his wife; it is you who has the right to test his mind, and ask him. Lead on — I will follow.'
